text_blocks.snippet: Xanthomas, which are cholesterol or fat deposits under the skin, are often treated by addressing the underlying medical condition causing them, along with potential surgical or laser removal of the lesions. If the xanthomas are a result of high blood lipid levels, treatment focuses on lowering those levels through lifestyle changes, medications, or both. Surgical removal or laser ablation can be used for symptomatic or cosmetically concerning lesions, but xanthomas may recur after these procedures.
snippet_highlighted_words: addressing the underlying medical condition causing them, along with potential surgical or laser removal of the lesions

list.snippet: Many xanthomas, like eruptive, tuberous, and palmar xanthomas, are linked to elevated blood lipid levels. Treating the underlying condition (e.g., high cholesterol, hypertriglyceridemia) with lifestyle changes (diet, exercise) and/or medications (statins, fibrates, etc.) can help reduce the appearance of xanthomas.
